name: Jade Varga

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What is a typical day at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and lead the fresh-food allocation team for a large supermarket company. We decide how much produce goes to each store and how quickly to mark down what will spoil. I have an MBA and know our growers, store managers and delivery limits well enough to spot when a tidy forecast makes no practical sense. I use AI forecasting every day, then ring a store when the pattern looks odd.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does work fit with home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband is an electrician and our children are eleven and sixteen. We have a mortgage and about three months of expenses saved, so an income gap would matter, though we could absorb a short one. My pay is typical for this level, and there are some buying and distribution jobs in the area. I like using the tool, but I do not want a store worker blamed for following a bad allocation from my screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At work I would say the modest AI forecast helps with tedious checks, but the store manager still has to tell us when the crates arrive bruised. The company should count food thrown away, not only how accurately a chart predicted sales.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my post is fairly safe if AI Plateau is all that happens. My husband has regular electrical jobs and we have three months saved, though the mortgage does not pause when either wage does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep a weekly call with the five stores that have the most waste and compare their notes with our forecast. I would continue our usual transfer to savings after both wages and the mortgage clear. If the mild change settles in during 2027, I would keep the call and adjust quantities when a store actually reports a problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own job in this version. I would still be irritated if a good forecast score hid bins full of strawberries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which store problem stays invisible in a forecast?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A store manager rang about six crates of soft strawberries arriving after the school fair was over. Our strawberry forecast read last year’s school fair sales and wanted more crates, even after this year’s fair ended. We moved the next load to a different shop instead of asking staff to sell spoiled fruit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you switch off the model?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would give the team the store note and change the assumption that caused the order. We can make a useful tool answer to the people who open the crates.

say: The **modest forecast** helps checks, while store reports should still change orders.
I would track **food waste** alongside forecast accuracy.
think: My **manager post** looks steady if change stays mild.
Our **mortgage and savings** still depend on both wages.
do: **Keep** weekly calls with five high-waste stores in 2026 and after arrival.
**Compare** store notes with forecasts and adjust reported bad orders.
**Continue** ordinary savings transfers after both wages and mortgage clear.
feel: I feel **calm** about my job but irritated by waste hidden in scores.
S0.quote: Our strawberry forecast read last year’s school fair sales and wanted more crates, even after this year’s fair ended.
fieldNote: Her **daily AI use** is grounded in produce allocation rather than a plan to retrain.
A **three-month reserve** supports calm in this mild case while both incomes remain relevant.

steps.text: Keep weekly calls with five stores reporting the most waste
Compare store notes with forecasts and adjust bad orders
Continue usual savings transfer after both wages and mortgage clear

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team that stronger automation can cut ordering work and possibly our headcount. I would publish the spoiled-stock and late-delivery numbers beside the software saving, because cutting a buyer without fixing delivery merely moves the mess into stores.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Off the record, I think one manager could be made responsible for several buying teams, including mine. I can work with AI and have an MBA, but neither makes my salary guaranteed. Three months saved is useful for a short search, not a long gap on a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the distribution director for a paid four-week trial handling produce quality complaints with one of my staff covering the allocation desk. I would do the trial only if the director approves the cover and my salary stays whole. As the change spreads, I would apply for posted supplier-quality roles that have pay after travel and shifts that work with our household rota; I would accept only a confirmed offer after checking those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious when I imagine the team shrinking. The evidence work interests me, but a promising title cannot pay the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you measure in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare what the grower said was packed with what our loading photographs and store returns show. Last month one pallet was warm before the lorry left the depot. The forecast had no reason to spot that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why take a quality role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It keeps me close to a product and to decisions that can be checked at a loading bay. It also gives me a chance to challenge a supplier properly. I would not trade away a steady salary merely for that chance.

say: **Ordering automation** may shrink teams unless waste and late deliveries count too.
I would publish **supplier evidence** beside software savings.
think: Several buying teams could fall under **one manager**, putting my salary at risk.
My **three-month reserve** covers a short search, not a long mortgage gap.
do: **Request** a four-week paid quality trial only with director-approved desk cover and full salary.
**Apply** for posted supplier-quality roles with viable net pay and household shifts.
**Accept** only a confirmed offer after checking travel costs, wages and rota.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a smaller team despite interest in quality work.
S1.quote: Last month one pallet was warm before the lorry left the depot.
fieldNote: The **quality trial** is conditional on approved cover and continued full salary, not an appointment already held.
Some **local vacancies** offer options, but household wages and shift fit still govern acceptance.

steps.text: Request four-week quality trial only with director-approved desk cover and full salary
Apply for posted supplier-quality roles with viable net wages and household shifts
Accept confirmed offer only after checking pay after travel and household rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the store managers AGI by 2028 could take our ordering, supplier letters and quality reports before anyone has designed replacement jobs. We would need written staffing dates and someone with authority to stop a bad load, not a vague promise that retail always needs people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my allocation seat might disappear quickly. Supplier-quality paperwork is thinking work too and faces the same 2028 date. Handling crates and checking temperatures stay physical longer, until robots around 2031, but I cannot assume those jobs will be waiting for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next week I would ask our worker forum for the actual severance and redeployment terms and send my CV to two posted local quality roles if their salary and shifts could meet the mortgage and family rota. I would not resign on an interview. If AGI arrives in 2028, I would accept a quality job only with a confirmed offer and pay after travel that covers our bills; I would check its contract and real loading-bay authority before moving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because a quick loss of this salary would run through our reserve. I also feel angry at the thought of store staff inheriting errors they are not allowed to correct.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the electrician income carry the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not by itself. My husband’s work is reasonably regular, but three months of savings would disappear quickly with this mortgage. We need both incomes or a deliberate smaller-bills plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does authority mean at the depot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a lorry arrives warm, the quality manager needs the right to hold the delivery while someone checks it. A title that only writes a report after the crates reach stores will not protect anyone.

say: **2028 AGI** could remove ordering and quality paperwork before replacement posts exist.
I would demand **staffing dates** and authority to hold unsafe loads.
think: My **allocation seat** and a supplier-quality desk both face 2028 thinking automation.
Physical crate checks face **2031 robots**, and no loading-bay vacancy is promised.
do: **Ask** the worker forum next week for written severance and redeployment terms.
**Apply** for two posted local roles only with viable salary and family-compatible shifts.
**Accept** after 2028 only a confirmed offer with bill-covering net pay and real hold authority.
feel: I feel **anxious** about salary loss and angry about uncorrectable store errors.
S2.quote: A title that only writes a report after the crates reach stores will not protect anyone.
fieldNote: She rejects **false refuge** in supplier-quality paperwork, which AGI could also perform by 2028.
Her **moderate reserve** offers a short search, while physical depot work is also exposed to 2031 robots.

steps.text: Ask worker forum next week for written severance and redeployment terms
Apply to two posted roles only with viable salary and family-compatible shifts
Accept confirmed offer after 2028 only with bill-covering net pay and load-hold authority

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to test the gap between a forecast and a real crate, but it does not make allocation jobs safe. I would ask the company to publish which decisions are left with staff as AGI approaches 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could use the time to become better at tracing a bad load from grower to store. I cannot count on a new quality desk after 2031, because its records and emails are also thinking work. By then the younger child will be sixteen, so the rota will be different, but our mortgage still needs a dependable wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I would lead two paid loading-bay investigations a quarter if the director approves time away from allocation and pays my full salary. I would take the food-safety qualification only if the company pays the fee and gives paid study hours, and I would complete it rather than just ask about a place. After 2031 I would apply only to an advertised role with actual stop-load authority and net wages that cover our mortgage and travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the desk job, but more able to test a different skill in five years than in two. The qualification would only matter if I can use it on real loads.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What counts as a real investigation?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The grower’s packing record, the lorry temperature and the store’s photograph all have to agree. I want to stand there when staff decide whether to refuse a delivery. Reading the AI summary at my desk would not teach that judgment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if they fund only the exam fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would hold off. I cannot leave my allocation team uncovered for unpaid study while the mortgage runs. A paid hour matters as much as a paid exam.

say: **2031 AGI** requires published decision rights, not only training adverts.
I would test **real load investigations** before claiming a new skill.
think: Quality records and allocation plans both face **2031 thinking automation**.
My **younger child** will be sixteen then, but dependable mortgage pay still matters.
do: **Lead** two paid load investigations quarterly from 2027 only with director-approved cover and full salary.
**Complete** food-safety qualification only with employer-paid fee and paid study hours.
**Apply** after 2031 only for advertised stop-load authority and mortgage-covering net pay.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk work but able to test practical judgment.
S3.quote: A paid hour matters as much as a paid exam.
fieldNote: Her **investigations** are conditional paid work with cover, not an assumed new job.
The **exam and hours** have separate gates; she commits to finish only if both are funded.

steps.text: Lead paid load investigations from 2027 only with director-approved cover and full salary
Complete food-safety qualification only with employer-paid fee and paid study hours
Apply after 2031 only for advertised load-hold authority and mortgage-covering net pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a decade is enough to argue for contracts that say who can refuse a bad delivery and what that work pays. I would not call a dashboard a future job simply because someone has given it a title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think the mortgage may be smaller by 2036, and the children will be adults, but I cannot spend that future saving today. Allocation, quality reports and supplier negotiation all face 2036 AGI. Hands-on loading checks face capable robots around 2039, so I need real pay and authority rather than a promise of permanent safety.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep calling stores about waste now and put thirty extra into savings only in months when both wages arrive and the mortgage and school costs clear. From 2028 I would seek a paid supplier dispute assignment only if the director approves cover and my salary remains whole. After 2036 I would stay in a load-quality job only while it has actual hold authority and wages that pay our bills; otherwise I would use the reserve to search posted openings rather than pretend the title protects me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about making a ten-year plan around jobs that may be different. I can act on the waste and the cash buffer now without claiming to know what work will exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will the older child still need school costs in 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, both children will be grown by then. The thirty extra is a decision for our current school and mortgage budget, not a claim that their costs stay the same for a decade. We would recalculate before any future move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a dispute assignment useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A grower once disputed a rejected batch because our temperature log had a missing hour. I would have to hear the driver and store manager before signing the refusal. That is more useful than practising another dashboard.

say: A **decade** allows clearer contracts for pay and refusal authority.
I would question a **dashboard title** without real load decisions.
think: The **2036 mortgage** may be smaller, but I cannot count that saving today.
Supplier negotiations face **2036 AGI**, while physical checks face robots around 2039.
do: **Save** thirty extra only after both wages, mortgage and current school costs clear.
**Seek** paid supplier disputes only with approved cover and full salary; stay after 2036 only with load-hold authority and bill-paying wages.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant work but able to address waste and savings now.
S4.quote: A grower once disputed a rejected batch because our temperature log had a missing hour.
fieldNote: Her **school costs** are current; both children are adults by 2036.
A **supplier dispute assignment** requires paid time and cover, while post-2036 retention requires real authority and wages.

steps.text: Keep weekly store calls about produce waste
Save thirty extra only after both wages mortgage and school costs clear
Seek paid supplier disputes only with director-approved cover and full salary
Stay after 2036 only with real load-hold authority and bill-paying wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. My allocation seat and a supplier-quality desk could both be lost before a new job is defined. A written staffing plan, genuine load-hold authority and paid time to investigate real deliveries would help us prepare; a course fee alone would not cover my working hours.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You should ask the store manager who has to open the delivery when the forecast is wrong. The crate matters more than the chart. A good forecast needs the person opening that crate to tell us when it is wrong.

headlineQuote: The crate matters more than the chart.
portrait: **Jade, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior fresh-food allocation manager at a large supermarket company.
Her **typical pay**, electrician husband, three-month reserve and some nearby roles support a mortgage and two children.
She uses **AI daily** for forecasts but listens to growers, drivers and store managers when the output fails.
She is **calm** under mild change and anxious about faster loss of her desk salary and team.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her allocation work before a paid role with real load authority exists.
whatWouldHelp: A written **staffing plan**, funded qualification and paid time on real load investigations would help.
